Pharmacology diagrams

Dextromethorphan metabolism & CYP2D6 interactions

DXM is O-demethylated by CYP2D6 to dextrorphan (DXO) and N-demethylated by CYP3A4 to 3-methoxymorphinan. Unlike risperidone, parent and metabolite are not equipotent — blocking CYP2D6 changes the drug you are actually giving. That conversion is used on purpose in Nuedexta and Auvelity, and happens by accident with fluoxetine or paroxetine. All four figures are embedded. This file works offline.

1. Pathway 2. Phenotypes 3. DDI cascade 4. Interaction map Intent table

01 Hepatic metabolism pathway

CYP2D6 O-demethylation is the rate-limiting, genetically polymorphic step. Both branches later meet at 3-hydroxymorphinan and UGT glucuronides. Urinary DXM/DXO is the classic CYP2D6 probe ratio.

DXM (parent). Sigma-1 agonist and serotonin-reuptake blocker. Weak NMDA antagonist. Antitussive at OTC doses.
DXO (metabolite). Much stronger uncompetitive NMDA antagonist. Dominates exposure in extensive metabolizers after first-pass.

02 CYP2D6 phenotype

Extensive metabolizers clear DXM in 2–4 hours; after a cough dose the parent is often undetectable. Poor metabolizers keep DXM for ~19–30 hours. The brain sees a different molecule in each group.

EM (~90%). Fast first-pass to DXO. Low urinary DXM/DXO ratio. Effect leans NMDA.
PM (~7–10%). Parent survives first-pass. High urinary DXM/DXO ratio. Effect leans σ1 + SERT.

03 Drug–drug interaction cascade

Fluoxetine, paroxetine, bupropion and quinidine all strongly inhibit CYP2D6 and convert an EM into a PM-like phenotype. Quinidine and bupropion are formulated with DXM on purpose. Fluoxetine and paroxetine are not.

PK result. ↑ DXM, ↓ DXO, t½ of parent stretches toward ~13–20 h, BID dosing becomes possible. Accidental stack of OTC DXM + an SSRI ± another 2D6 inhibitor raises serotonin-syndrome and dissociation risk.

04 Interaction map

Intended pairs: Nuedexta (DXM 20 mg + quinidine 10 mg BID for PBA) and Auvelity (DXM 45 mg + bupropion 105 mg for MDD). Accidental pairs: cough syrup plus fluoxetine or paroxetine.
